page_title: Haze Marijuana Strain - Kind Green Buds

source_page_metadata.description: Explore the Haze marijuana strain - THC levels, genetics, terpene profile, effects, flavor, and grow tips.

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Pure Sativa
Breeder: The Haze Brothers (Santa Cruz, California)
Genetics: Colombian × Mexican × Thai × South Indian
THC Content: ~16–20% (varies widely by phenotype)
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Limonene , Caryophyllene
Flowering Time (Indoor): 12–16 weeks
Harvest Time (Outdoor): Late October to November
Yield (Indoor): Moderate
Yield (Outdoor): Moderate to High in warm climates
Plant Height: Tall
Difficulty: Difficult

Few cannabis cultivars have influenced modern breeding as profoundly as Haze . Emerging from the counterculture era of the early 1970s in Santa Cruz, California, the strain represents one of the earliest successful attempts to combine multiple tropical sativa landraces into a single hybrid. The resulting plant captured the imagination of growers and consumers alike, not only for its distinctive effects but also for its unusual growth patterns and aromatic complexity.

Unlike many contemporary hybrids bred primarily for speed or yield, this cultivar evolved from patient experimentation. Early breeders carefully selected plants that expressed intense cerebral effects, unusual terpene profiles, and vibrant growth characteristics. The result was a strain that quickly became the foundation for countless modern varieties. Today, many famous cultivars—including Super Silver Haze , Neville’s Haze , and Amnesia Haze —trace their lineage back to this pioneering genetic line.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic foundation of Haze reflects a blend of several equatorial landrace strains collected during the global cannabis exploration of the 1960s and early 1970s. According to historical accounts associated with the Haze Brothers of Santa Cruz, the earliest versions combined Colombian and Mexican sativas. These plants provided the first layer of the hybrid’s energetic mental effects and citrus-leaning terpene profile.

Further refinement introduced genetics from Southeast Asia and India, specifically Thai and South Indian landraces. These additions transformed the plant dramatically. Thai cannabis contributed elongated flowering structures and extremely uplifting cerebral effects, while the South Indian genetics helped stabilize growth and increase resin production. Together, these four regional influences created a plant that expressed a uniquely global genetic heritage.

Over time, breeders across Europe began working with the strain to refine its characteristics. Notably, Dutch breeder Neville Schoenmakers incorporated the genetics into breeding programs that ultimately produced many modern haze hybrids. While the original version is relatively rare today, its genetic blueprint continues to shape a vast number of contemporary cannabis cultivars.
Effects and Experience

The psychoactive experience produced by this cultivar often unfolds in stages rather than arriving all at once. Early onset typically manifests as a sharp increase in mental clarity. Thoughts may appear more fluid, and creative ideas often emerge more easily. Rather than inducing immediate relaxation, the strain initially stimulates awareness and sensory perception.

As the experience deepens, a noticeable shift in mood frequently accompanies the cerebral stimulation. Many individuals describe a sense of lightness or elevated perspective that can make everyday activities feel more engaging. Social interaction tends to flow more naturally during this phase, making the strain appealing for conversation, creative collaboration, or exploration of new ideas.

Later in the experience, subtle physical sensations begin to develop. Instead of heavy sedation, the body often experiences a gentle release of tension. Muscles relax slightly while mental alertness remains intact. This balance allows the energetic qualities of the strain to persist without becoming overwhelming, creating an experience that feels both stimulating and harmonious.
Medical Benefits

Cannabis varieties with strong sativa heritage often attract interest from individuals seeking mental stimulation rather than physical sedation. In the case of this cultivar, the clear-headed cerebral effects may help support focus and motivation during periods of fatigue or low energy. Some patients find that the strain encourages productivity and mental engagement, particularly during daytime hours.

Mood elevation is another reason this plant appears in many therapeutic discussions. The uplifting nature of its effects may assist individuals coping with stress or negative thought patterns. Rather than simply dulling emotional discomfort, the strain’s energetic mental character can sometimes promote a more optimistic outlook or renewed sense of curiosity.

While the hybrid leans heavily toward cerebral stimulation, mild physical comfort often accompanies the later stages of the experience. This gentle relaxation may help reduce minor muscle tension without impairing mobility. For individuals seeking a balance between mental uplift and light physical relief, the plant can offer a unique therapeutic profile.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aromatic signature of this cultivar is among the most distinctive in cannabis history . When the dried flower is broken apart, a sharp burst of spice and citrus frequently fills the air. Terpinolene contributes bright herbal notes, while limonene adds a layer of fresh citrus reminiscent of lemon peel. Together, these compounds create a scent that feels both invigorating and complex.

Beyond the initial brightness, deeper aromatic tones gradually emerge. Subtle hints of wood, incense, and sweet earthiness can often be detected when the buds are examined more closely. Caryophyllene introduces a peppery warmth, while pinene adds a faint forest-like freshness. This layered terpene combination produces an aroma that feels vibrant yet grounded.

During consumption, the flavor tends to follow a similar progression. The first inhale often carries herbal citrus notes accompanied by a light sweetness. As the vapor or smoke lingers on the palate, a gentle spice and woody character becomes more pronounced. The lingering aftertaste frequently retains a touch of citrus alongside subtle herbal complexity.
Growing Information

Growing this cultivar presents a unique set of challenges compared to many modern hybrids. The plant exhibits classic equatorial sativa growth patterns, meaning it develops tall stems and extended branches that can stretch significantly during flowering. Indoor growers often employ training techniques such as topping or screen-of-green methods to manage height and maximize canopy coverage.

Flowering time represents one of the most distinctive traits of the strain . Unlike many contemporary varieties that finish within eight to ten weeks, this plant often requires twelve to fourteen weeks to fully mature. Although the extended flowering period demands patience, it allows the plant to develop complex terpene profiles and distinctive elongated bud structures.

Outdoor cultivation tends to produce the most impressive results when the plant is grown in warm climates with long growing seasons. In these environments, it can reach considerable heights and produce airy yet resinous flowers along extended branches. Proper airflow and sunlight are essential for maintaining healthy growth throughout the long flowering cycle.
FAQ

What kind of strain is Haze? It is a sativa-dominant hybrid derived from multiple tropical landrace strains including Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and South Indian genetics. The strain is famous for its energetic cerebral effects.

How strong is Haze? THC levels typically range from about 16% to 22%. While potency can vary depending on cultivation and phenotype, the effects are usually described as mentally stimulating rather than physically heavy.

Why is Haze historically important? The strain became one of the foundational genetic lines used in modern cannabis breeding. Many well-known varieties, including Super Silver Haze and Amnesia Haze, descend from its lineage.
Is Haze good for daytime use? Many people prefer it earlier in the day due to its energizing mental effects. The strain often promotes alertness and creativity rather than sedation.

Is Haze difficult to grow? Cultivating this plant can be challenging because of its tall growth pattern and long flowering time. Growers with experience managing sativa varieties often achieve the best results.
Final Thoughts on Haze

Few cannabis cultivars have achieved the legendary status of Haze. Developed during an era when experimentation and exploration shaped the cannabis landscape, the strain helped define the modern concept of a complex sativa hybrid. Its combination of global landrace genetics produced a plant unlike anything seen before at the time.

The hybrid’s impact continues to ripple through the cannabis world decades later. Countless modern strains rely on its genetics to deliver energetic cerebral effects and distinctive terpene profiles. Even when the original version is not directly encountered, its influence remains present in many of the most celebrated cultivars available today.

For enthusiasts interested in the history of cannabis genetics, exploring this strain offers a glimpse into the roots of modern breeding. Its lively mental stimulation, intricate aroma, and distinctive growth characteristics reflect a time when cultivators patiently shaped plants through careful selection rather than rapid hybridization. In many ways, Haze remains one of the defining pillars of contemporary cannabis culture.
